title: /kb-autopilot runs the backlog as a manager loop
goal: The /kb-autopilot skill, run in its own clone under /loop, does one tick from autopilot.py status: intake --file --network and triage of its drafts, review, retrospective and close of each runner that exited (provisional answers confirmed and retro stories picked as autopilot decisions), refill to two runners (plan, research, start, runner start), the digest, and a PushNotification only for gates the operator keeps; judgment steps run in subagents that return a short JSON, the skill holds Compact Instructions, and it never writes auto-memory

gates.question: How does the manager reach the operator?
options: push notification for kept gates plus the committed digest
gates.recommendation: push notification for kept gates plus the committed digest
gates.answer: push notification for kept gates plus the committed digest; the manager runs as a local loop session in its own clone

gates.question: Does the manager run as one interactive /loop session with compaction hooks, or as a Python outer loop launching a fresh claude -p per tick?
options: interactive /loop session first, generational ticks if rot metrics show drift
gates.recommendation: interactive /loop session first, generational ticks if rot metrics show drift
gates.answer: interactive /loop session first, generational ticks if rot metrics show drift

notes: From ST-fb2hxf6s: the manager's dispatch must call backlog.py procs --record for the runner's processes (autopilot.py was outside that story's touches); the tick runs procs and ends only an owned orphan after the grace.
